title: Introducing Inkling 2 Mini - Thinking Machines Lab

quotes.for: Publication date of the release post.

quotes.text: Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token.
quotes.for: Looped architecture running middle layers three times per token.

quotes.text: Inkling 2 Mini leads every open-weights model with less than 100B total parameters on benchmarks such as DeepSWE v1.1 (48.2%) and Vals Index v2.2 (46.5%).
quotes.for: DeepSWE v1.1 and Vals Index v2.2 benchmark scores.

quotes.text: Inkling 2 Mini is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 26.4B total parameters, 3.4B active, and 5.4B weight activations per token to account for looping.
quotes.for: Total, active, and looped weight activation parameter counts.

quotes.text: Most of Inkling 2 Mini’s weights were trained and are deployed natively in NVFP4, with the last four layers in MXFP8.
quotes.for: NVFP4 and MXFP8 precision details.

quotes.text: The total memory footprint of Inkling 2 Mini is ~20GB, allowing it to run on local devices such as consumer laptops and desktop AI computers.
quotes.for: 20 GB memory footprint and local device support.

quotes.text: At launch we support Inkling 2 Mini running on any Mac system (MacBook, Mac Mini) with at least 32GB RAM via Ollama.
quotes.for: Mac 32 GB RAM and Ollama support at launch.

quotes.text: While looping improves the model’s reasoning, it doesn’t enable its weights to store more facts—knowledge is mostly a function of total parameter count.
quotes.for: Looping does not increase factual storage.

quotes.text: Reasoning at 5 passes was less than half as long as at 1 pass (1,661 vs. 3,703 tokens on average), but no less legible: sentence length and the fraction of words in an English dictionary were unchanged.
quotes.for: Token length reduction and unchanged legibility across 5 passes vs 1 pass.

title: Thinking Machines has released Inkling 2 Mini, an open weights looped transformer

quotes.text: November 20, 2026
quotes.for: Publication date of the Artificial Analysis evaluation.

quotes.text: It is released under an Apache 2.0 license, with text and image input and a 1M token context window.
quotes.for: Apache 2.0 license, multimodal inputs, and 1M context window.

quotes.text: Inkling 2 Mini matches Qwen3.8 27B (xhigh) and Nanbeige4.3-33B on the Intelligence Index with ~5x and ~6x fewer active parameters, respectively.
quotes.for: Intelligence Index tie and active parameter comparison.

quotes.text: Inkling 2 Mini uses ~38% more output tokens than Qwen3.8 27B for the same Intelligence Index score, but ~2.8x less compute.
quotes.for: Output token and compute comparison against Qwen3.8 27B.

quotes.text: It costs $0.59 and takes 9.0 minutes per Intelligence Index task vs. $3.53 and 38.2 minutes for Qwen3.8 27B.
quotes.for: Cost and runtime per Intelligence Index task.

title: New open model Inkling 2 Mini thinks in loops to solve problems with fewer words and still runs on a laptop

quotes.for: Publication date of The Decoder article.

quotes.text: Inkling 2 Mini runs 12 of its 24 layers three times in a row.
quotes.for: 12 of 24 layers looped three times.

quotes.text: The open mixture-of-experts model has 26.4 billion parameters, with 5.4 billion active per token because of the loops, the company says.
quotes.for: MoE parameter counts and looping activation.

quotes.text: November 20, 2026
quotes.for: Publication date of the Goodfire research post.

quotes.text: Thinking Machines provided Goodfire with early access to the weights of Inkling 2 Mini so we could investigate how these architectural innovations affect the model’s internal mechanisms.
quotes.for: Early access to weights provided to Goodfire.

quotes.text: Our preliminary findings include insights into how layers coordinate with each other, and with future and past versions of themselves: counterintuitively, looped model layers can write to themselves, or read from “future” layers!
quotes.for: Layer coordination across loops including writing to themselves and reading from future layers.
